proposed.explanation: While Mesopotamian palaces did feature courtyard plans (as seen in Hammurabi's palace), Sennacherib's palace is specifically noted for its sculptured gateways and relief programs. Concrete vaults are a Roman innovation, not Mesopotamian. Mesopotamian architecture used mud brick, not concrete. Hypostyle halls are characteristic of Egyptian and Persian architecture, not Mesopotamian palaces, which featured courtyards and relief-decorated walls. The palace of Sennacherib at Nineveh (705–681 BCE) included monumental gateways guarded by sculptured figures (lamassu—winged bull and lion hybrids) and extensive relief programs narrating royal hunts and military victories.'
